subChunks.title: v3 to v4 Migration
subChunks.hookHtml: Migrating a production Tailwind v3 codebase to v4 is a high-stakes operation. Classes renamed. Config model replaced. PostCSS setup changed. A careless migration breaks thousands of classes across hundreds of files. A systematic migration — running the automated tool, understanding what it can and can't fix, then addressing the manual changes — takes a large codebase from v3 to v4 without regressions.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Maester Cordell: "Do not migrate in production. Do not migrate without a complete test suite baseline. The automated tool handles ~90% of the work — class renames, config moves, PostCSS updates. The remaining 10% requires judgment: plugin compatibility, custom utility patterns, and anything that touched the JS config in ways the tool cannot infer."

Step 1: Run the automated migration tool

npx @tailwindcss/upgrade

# The tool:
# 1. Updates tailwind and PostCSS dependencies
# 2. Converts tailwind.config.js → CSS @theme
# 3. Renames deprecated class names
# 4. Updates PostCSS config
# 5. Adds @import "tailwindcss" to your CSS entry

Breaking changes: renamed utilities

/* Colour palette renames */
v3 → v4
shadow-sm        → shadow-xs
shadow           → shadow-sm
shadow-md        → shadow      (default)
ring-0           → ring-0 (unchanged)
blur             → blur-sm
blur-sm          → blur-xs

/* Opacity utilities */
bg-opacity-50    → bg-black/50  (use / modifier)
text-opacity-75  → text-current with opacity modifier

/* Outline rename */
outline-none     → outline-hidden (v4)
                   (outline: none now literally means no outline — a11y risk)

Breaking changes: configuration

/* v3 tailwind.config.js */
module.exports = {
  content: ['./src/**/*.{ts,tsx,html}'],  // → @source in CSS
  darkMode: 'class',                       // → @variant dark in CSS
  theme: {
    extend: {
      colors: { brand: '#6366f1' },        // → @theme in CSS
      fontFamily: { sans: ['Inter'] },      // → @theme in CSS
    }
  },
  plugins: [require('@tailwindcss/forms')]  // → still in tailwind.config.js
};

What the tool cannot fix automatically

  • Custom plugin compatibility — v3 plugins that use the old API may need updating
  • JIT safelist patterns — safelist with regex patterns must become @source inline()
  • Complex theme() references — theme() in CSS that references extended values
  • CSS Modules with @apply — @apply behaviour changed slightly in v4
  • outline-none → outline-hidden — semantic change requires manual audit

The @apply change in v4

/* v3: @apply worked anywhere in CSS */
.my-component {
  @apply flex items-center gap-4 hover:bg-gray-100;
}

/* v4: @apply still works, but:
  - Variants in @apply (hover:) are expanded inline
  - Utilities must be generated before @apply can reference them
  - CSS Modules: may need extra configuration */

Testing your migration

# Before migration: capture visual baseline
npx percy snapshot dist/  # or Chromatic, Playwright screenshots

# Run migration
npx @tailwindcss/upgrade

# Build and compare
npm run build
# Compare CSS bundle size (should be similar or smaller)
# Run visual regression suite
# Run accessibility tests
npx axe-cli http://localhost:3000

Cordell: "The outline-none change is the most dangerous breaking change in v4 for accessibility. In v3, outline-none suppressed the browser's focus ring. In v4, outline-hidden suppresses it. If you missed this rename, your focus styles silently broke. Always check: every focus-visible: must have a corresponding outline-hidden or ring-* utility."

storyBeats.speaker: Maester Cordell
storyBeats.text: The migration tool handles the mechanical work — renames, config conversion, dependency updates. What it cannot do is reason about your intent. Was that outline-none suppressing a focus ring that you're replacing with focus-visible:? Or was it a mistake? That judgment is yours.

storyBeats.speaker: Critical rename: outline-none → outline-hidden

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml:
Build a migration checklist UI showing the v3→v4 breaking changes by category:

  • .mig-page: max-w-2xl, mx-auto, p-6, space-y-4
  • .mig-section: bg-white, rounded-xl, border, border-gray-200, overflow-hidden
  • .mig-section-header: flex, items-center, gap-2, px-4, py-3, bg-gray-50, border-b, border-gray-100
  • .mig-section-title: text-sm, font-semibold, text-gray-700
  • .mig-list: divide-y, divide-gray-100
  • .mig-item: flex, items-center, justify-between, px-4, py-2.5, text-sm
  • .mig-old: font-mono, text-red-600, line-through, text-xs
  • .mig-new: font-mono, text-emerald-700, text-xs

subChunks.soloPracticeHtml: Design a complete v3→v4 migration plan card from scratch. Include: automated tool command and what it covers, a table of the 5 most critical manual checks (outline-none, shadow renames, plugin audit, @apply in CSS Modules, JIT safelist), and a testing checklist (visual baseline, bundle size comparison, axe audit). No starter code.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Walk through the v3→v4 migration process step by step: what the automated tool does, what it cannot do, and the single most dangerous breaking change for accessibility. If a v3 codebase has 'outline-none' on buttons, what exactly breaks in v4 and how do you fix it?

questions.prompt: What does the npx @tailwindcss/upgrade command handle automatically during a v3→v4 migration?
options: Dependency updates, config conversion from tailwind.config.js to CSS @theme, class renames (shadow, blur, etc.), and PostCSS config updates
Only class renames — config and dependency changes require manual intervention
Only the PostCSS config — all other changes must be done manually
Everything including plugin compatibility and @apply audit — the migration is fully automated
questions.answer: Dependency updates, config conversion from tailwind.config.js to CSS @theme, class renames (shadow, blur, etc.), and PostCSS config updates
questions.explanation: The upgrade tool handles the mechanical, deterministic parts of migration: updating package versions, converting theme extend values to @theme blocks, renaming classes with known v3→v4 mappings (shadow-sm→shadow-xs, etc.), and updating the PostCSS or Vite config. It cannot handle cases that require intent judgment — plugin compatibility, complex theme() references, or semantic changes like outline-none.

questions.prompt: After migrating a v3 codebase to v4, keyboard focus indicators disappear on all buttons. The buttons used focus:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2. What happened and how do you fix it?
options: outline-none in v4 means literal CSS outline: none — the ring-2 never renders because the ring requires outline to be set. Fix: change focus:outline-none to focus:outline-hidden, which suppresses the native ring while allowing ring-* to render.
focus-visible:ring-2 is not supported in v4 — change it to focus:ring-2
The ring-2 class was renamed to ring in v4 — the ring disappeared because the class generates no CSS
The migration tool accidentally deleted all focus-visible: classes — rerun the migration
questions.answer: outline-none in v4 means literal CSS outline: none — the ring-2 never renders because the ring requires outline to be set. Fix: change focus:outline-none to focus:outline-hidden, which suppresses the native ring while allowing ring-* to render.
questions.explanation: This is the most impactful breaking change in v4. In v3, outline-none was a semantic utility that suppressed the browser's native focus outline while the developer provided a custom one (usually via ring-*). In v4, the semantic has changed: outline-hidden suppresses the native ring (matching v3's outline-none behavior), and outline-none literally sets outline: none — which conflicts with ring-* rendering. Every focus:outline-none must become focus:outline-hidden.

questions.prompt: A v3 project has safelist: [{ pattern: /^bg-/ }] in tailwind.config.js. The migration tool does not convert this automatically. What is the v4 equivalent?
options: @source inline("bg-{red,blue,green,indigo}-{100,200,300,400,500,600,700,800,900}") in the CSS file — listing the specific patterns needed rather than a broad regex
safelist: [/^bg-/] in tailwind.config.js still works in v4 — no change needed
There is no v4 equivalent — regex safelists must be converted to individual class names
questions.answer: @source inline("bg-{red,blue,green,indigo}-{100,200,300,400,500,600,700,800,900}") in the CSS file — listing the specific patterns needed rather than a broad regex
questions.explanation: v4 replaces regex safelist patterns with @source inline() using brace-expansion syntax. The migration requires understanding which specific classes the regex was meant to safelist and being precise rather than broad. A regex like /^bg-/ could match thousands of classes — @source inline() forces you to specify exactly which colour-shade combinations you need, which also prevents the performance anti-pattern of generating an enormous CSS file.
